disclaimer: These are illustrative, synthetic reference profiles built from the public NYHA heart failure functional classification and typical cardiac reference ranges. They are NOT real patient records and are NOT individually cited the way the drug PK table requires. Treat them as placeholder data to unblock rendering and simulation, and replace with reviewed, cited values before any claim beyond a hackathon demo.

field_notes.nyha_class: New York Heart Association functional class I (no symptoms) through IV (symptoms at rest), or 'none' for no heart failure
field_notes.lvef_pct: Left ventricular ejection fraction: the % of blood the left ventricle pumps out per beat; normal is roughly 55-70%
field_notes.cardiac_output_l_min: Blood pumped per minute; falls as the heart weakens
field_notes.mean_arterial_pressure_mmhg: Typical blood pressure state associated with this profile
field_notes.baseline_qt_interval_ms: Baseline QT interval on an ECG; a longer baseline means less safety margin before a QT-prolonging drug becomes dangerous
field_notes.contractility_multiplier: Relative multiplier used by the simulation for how strongly the heart muscle contracts (1.0 = normal); used to scale the effect of inotropic or cardiotoxic drugs
field_notes.conduction_sensitivity_multiplier: Relative sensitivity to drugs that affect heart rhythm or conduction (1.0 = normal; higher = more prone to arrhythmia from a given drug exposure)
field_notes.cardiotoxic_sensitivity_multiplier: Relative multiplier for how much a cardiotoxic drug damages or weakens this heart per unit exposure (1.0 = healthy baseline)

profiles.label: Healthy adult heart
profiles.basis: Standard healthy-adult reference ranges for LVEF, resting heart rate, cardiac output and QT interval

profiles.label: Hypertension with left ventricular hypertrophy, preserved ejection fraction
profiles.basis: NYHA class I means structural heart disease with no symptom limitation; ejection fraction is preserved despite the thickened muscle, which is the defining feature of this stage

profiles.label: Mild heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), NYHA II
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
profiles.basis: NYHA II is mild symptoms with ordinary activity; LVEF < 40% defines HFrEF

profiles.label: Moderate heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, NYHA III
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
profiles.basis: NYHA III is marked symptom limitation with less-than-ordinary activity; falling cardiac output and a longer baseline QT reflect the more compromised muscle

profiles.label: Severe heart failure post-myocardial infarction, NYHA IV
conditions: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
profiles.basis: NYHA IV is symptoms at rest; a prior infarction leaves a region of dead, non-contracting muscle (scar), which is why contractility drops sharply and arrhythmia risk from drugs rises further

profiles.label: Atrial fibrillation, otherwise preserved pump function
profiles.basis: Atrial fibrillation is primarily a rhythm disorder rather than a pump-strength problem, so LVEF and contractility stay closer to normal while conduction sensitivity is set high to reflect the existing electrical instability
